description:
Treat a file under an issue's resolved artifact directory as that issue's document by location, so that artifacts need an explicit link only when they live elsewhere or need metadata.

## Background

An issue's documents are discoverable today only when linked. `doc list` returns the issue's explicit links verbatim, the link checker's tracked set is built from those links, and the server's document content, history, diff and search routes require a link. Workers in linked worktrees therefore report a list of paths, and the lead links them after merging; a forgotten link costs a review round.

The artifact directory an issue owns is already resolved by the repository's layout, through a pure, configuration-driven resolver (`crates/jit/src/domain/artifact_directory.rs:62-108`; `[documentation].issue_scoped_areas`). An issue owns one directory per declared documentation area, so location alone says which issue a file belongs to. A repository that declares no areas derives nothing. A git-free recursive walk of a directory already exists (`crates/jit/src/storage/artifact_planning.rs`).

Artifact-layout conformance already attributes a path to an issue by its short-id prefix, without a link (`crates/jit/src/domain/artifact_conformance.rs:207-243`).

The design is one pure domain function that returns an issue's derived documents: the files under its resolved artifact directory in each declared area. Document listing, link checking and server document reads consume it. A derived document carries no type and no label. An explicit link remains the way to attach a path outside the directory, and the way to attach metadata such as the plan label to any path.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Listing an issue's documents includes every file under its resolved artifact directories without an explicit link.
- [hard] REQ-02: Link checking and the server's document reads treat such a file as tracked.
- [hard] REQ-04: Artifacts a worker commits in a linked worktree under the issue's artifact directory are listed as its documents once the branch merges, with no tracker write.
- [hard] REQ-05: One pure domain function returns an issue's derived documents, and a derived document carries no type or label.

## Notes

- Criterion ID REQ-03 is retired here. Removing redundant explicit links from existing records, and archiving derived documents with their issue, are separate work.
- Displaying an unpinned document reads it from the committed tree when a repository exists, so an uncommitted derived file is listed but cannot be displayed until it is committed.
title: Derive an issue's documents from its artifact directory
